transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Um, well, my mom is the one who made the appointment. She's just... she's really upset with me because mostly I just can't make myself do anything anymore. Like, nothing at all. I just sit in my room all day. I sit on the edge of my bed, and I've been wearing these exact same clothes—this same oversized hoodie and these pajama pants—for I don't even know how many days now. It's just... it takes too much to take them off, and there's no point anyway. 

I don't do any of the stuff I used to do. I used to knit all the time, I was working on this really complicated sweater with cables and everything, and the basket is just sitting right there on the floor, but I don't touch it. I don't touch my journals either, and I used to write pages and pages every single night with these special colored pens I bought. I don't even go out for walks around the neighborhood to get fresh air like I used to. I just sit there staring at the wall. 

And then my mom comes in, and she stands in the doorway and she keeps asking me, "What's wrong? Why are you acting like this? What's happening?" over and over, and she wants this big explanation about my feelings, but I just... I barely have the energy to even look at her, let alone answer. It's like my mouth is too heavy to move and my brain is just empty. So I just stay quiet, and I guess that's why she brought me here, because I just don't have the energy for anything at all.
Have you ever experienced a period of time, lasting at least a few days, where you felt unusually energetic, talkative, or euphoric, to the point where you didn't feel like you needed much sleep?

No, I... I don't think so. I mean, I can't really imagine feeling like that, not right now anyway. Energetic? Euphoric? It's just... it's so far away from how I feel. Like, I told you about how I just sit on the edge of my bed in these same clothes, right? The hoodie and the pajama pants. I just sit there. And sleep... sleep is weird because I don't really feel rested, but I definitely don't feel like I *don't* need it. I just feel heavy all the time. 

I don't think I've ever had a time where I was just talking and talking and not sleeping and feeling amazing. Even when I was doing okay, like when I was working on that cabled sweater—the one in the basket on my floor that I haven't touched in forever—or when I was writing in my journals with all those different colored pens every night, I wasn't, like, bouncing off the walls or anything. I was just... doing things. Normal things. And I slept normally, I think. I didn't stay up for days on end feeling like I could take on the world. 

My mom would definitely remember if I had done that, anyway. She notices everything. Like how she keeps standing in my doorway asking me what's wrong and wanting me to explain my feelings when I just... I can't. If I had been running around the house not sleeping and talking a mile a minute, she would have brought it up, or she would have brought me here sooner. But no, it's just been this... this heaviness. This emptiness. So, no, I've never felt like what you're describing. Not for a few days, not for one day. Just... never.
Have you ever gone through a period like this in the past, where you felt this same level of heaviness and loss of interest for several weeks or more?

Um, no... I really don't think so. I mean, not like this. I was in high school not that long ago, and sure, I had days where I was tired, like everyone gets tired when they have to study or do homework or whatever. But it wasn't this... this intense gravity. Like, right now, just sitting here, my arms literally feel like they are made out of wet cement. I have never had a time in my life where I couldn't even bring myself to pick up a pen. I told you about those colored pens, right? The special ones I bought for my journals. I used to use them every single night without fail. Even if I had a really bad week or was super stressed out about finishing school, I always wrote pages and pages. 

And my mom, she wouldn't be acting so confused and upset if this had ever happened before. She keeps standing in my doorway, asking me what is wrong and why I am acting like this, because she has never seen me just sitting on the edge of my bed in this exact same oversized hoodie for days on end. If I had gone through a period like this before, she would probably say something like, oh, you are doing that thing again, let us get you help. But she doesn't say that. She acts like I am a completely alien person that she doesn't even recognize. 

So it has to be the first time. Because I definitely don't remember feeling this incredibly empty, and she clearly doesn't remember it either. I just... I really don't know how everything got so heavy. It just sort of crept up on me and now I am completely stuck in these pajama pants and I can't even look at the knitting basket. It is just sitting there on the floor mocking me. I have never in my life abandoned a sweater before, especially not one with cables. Cables are really hard to do, you have to count all the stitches and keep careful track of the rows, and I was so good at it. I would never just leave it on the floor gathering dust if I didn't have to. So no, I haven't had a time like this. Never anything this heavy.
